topics.name: DMZ Design
practices: Separate internet-facing services from internal applications.
Use reverse proxies or load balancers to terminate public traffic.
Restrict management access to DMZ assets through jump hosts.
Log all north-south flows and validate rule changes through change control.

topics.name: Network Segmentation
practices: Group systems by trust, function, and sensitivity.
Default-deny east-west traffic and allow only required ports.
Use dedicated management, backup, and monitoring networks.
Review segmentation effectiveness with packet captures and tests.

topics.name: Privileged Access Management
practices: Vault shared credentials and rotate them automatically.
Prefer just-in-time elevation over standing admin access.
Record privileged sessions for high-risk systems.
Review privileged roles and service accounts on a scheduled cadence.

topics.name: SIEM Operations
practices: Normalize logs before building detections.
Track alert fidelity and suppress known noisy conditions.
Map detections to MITRE ATT&CK and business impact.
Continuously validate ingestion coverage from critical assets.

topics.name: Incident Response
practices: Keep playbooks short, actionable, and owner-assigned.
Run tabletop exercises for ransomware and cloud account compromise.
Protect evidence and preserve timelines during investigations.
Capture lessons learned and update detections after each exercise or incident.

topics.name: System Hardening
practices: Disable unused services, ports, and local administrator accounts.
Apply CIS-aligned baselines to servers and network devices.
Enforce MFA, SSH key policies, and password rotation.
Patch operating systems, hypervisors, and firmware in scheduled windows.

topics.name: Firewall Rules
practices: Implement least-privilege allow rules with documented ownership.
Separate temporary rules and review them for expiration.
Log denied traffic for sensitive segments and internet edges.
Validate rule sets against actual application flows before promotion.

topics.name: Logging & Retention
practices: Use synchronized time across collectors and endpoints.
Protect log pipelines against tampering and data loss.
Define retention by regulatory need and incident response requirements.
Test restore and search of archived logs before an emergency occurs.
